card.title: Preserve the release. Pursue the record.
card.summary: A local-first desktop system for syncing, preserving, searching, analyzing, and exporting public UAP records.

hero.title: Preserve the release. Pursue the record.
hero.summary: A polished, independent desktop companion for syncing, preserving, searching, analyzing, and exporting the public records released through the Department of War PURSUE portal.

project.independence_notice: PURSUE Data Analyzer is an independent open-source analysis tool. It is not produced, endorsed, or operated by the U.S. Department of War or any other government agency. References to WAR.gov describe the public source material the application can sync and preserve.

sections.capabilities_lead: The official portal publishes the source material. PURSUE turns those public releases into a durable, searchable working library without sending your evidence to a hosted analysis service.
sections.workflow_lead: The normal workflow is deliberately simple. You stay in control of what is synced, downloaded, analyzed, and exported.
sections.builds_lead: Stable URLs always resolve to the current digest-verified release. GitHub retains the authoritative release history.
sections.support_lead: Everything needed to choose, install, and trust the correct build—without burying the important caveats.
sections.integrity_lead: Compare the SHA-256 for the file you downloaded. The mirror verifies these values against GitHub before stable download links advance.

lanes.label: macOS 26+ // Apple Silicon required
lanes.title: Metal acceleration
lanes.body: For M-series Macs running macOS 26 or newer. Open the DMG, move PURSUE to Applications, and launch it from there. Intel Macs and older macOS releases are not supported by the current build.

lanes.label: Windows 10/11 x64 // NVIDIA Turing or newer
lanes.title: CUDA lane
lanes.body: Includes the pinned NVIDIA runtime for local GPU acceleration. No separate CUDA toolkit is required. This package is intentionally large and MSI-only.

lanes.label: Windows 10/11 x64 // AMD, Intel, or unsure
lanes.title: DirectML lane
lanes.body: The broad-compatibility choice for non-NVIDIA hardware. Use the setup EXE for a normal installation; the MSI is available for managed deployment.
lanes.build_detail: EXE / AMD, Intel, and broad GPU support

support_notes.title: How do I install PURSUE on macOS?
support_notes.body: Requires macOS 26 or newer on Apple Silicon (M-series), matching the current release build target. Open the DMG and move PURSUE to Applications. Apple may show a Gatekeeper warning until Developer ID notarization is configured; verify this domain and the SHA-256 first, then use Privacy & Security → Open Anyway if needed.

support_notes.title: Which PURSUE installer should I use on Windows?
support_notes.body: Requires 64-bit Windows 10 or 11. Use CUDA for a supported NVIDIA GPU; use DirectML for AMD, Intel, other GPUs, or when unsure. SmartScreen may warn until Authenticode signing is configured; verify the hostname and checksum before choosing More info → Run anyway.

support_notes.title: Where does PURSUE store data, and what network access does it use?
support_notes.body: Your database, evidence library, snapshots, models, notes, and exports remain in the operating-system app-data directory. Network access is used for official source/evidence downloads, release checks, and model downloads you initiate. PURSUE does not require hosted OCR, hosted embeddings, or a paid AI API.

support_notes.title: Are PURSUE updates signed, and will an update preserve my data?
support_notes.body: Production update bundles are signed with the Tauri updater key. Updates and reinstalls preserve the database, evidence vault, models, exports, resumable downloads, and custom-storage pointer. Operating-system trust warnings are separate from updater signatures. GitHub remains the release source of truth; this R2 mirror publishes the same digest-verified bytes.
